8160.en: The points X_8160 and X_8161 are labeled Z_{1} and Z_{2}, respectively, in this sketch: **X_8160 and X_8161** (``X_8160andX(8161).png``).

ba.t: a^2 (SA - (S Sin[ω]) / (2 + Cos[ω])) : : Let ABC be a triangle, and let A'B'C' be the cevian triangle of X_6. Let U be the line through A' parallel to AB, and let V be the line through A' parallel to AC. Let U' = U∩AC and V' = V∩AB. The 4 points B, C, U', V' lie on a circle, (O) _A. Define (O) _B and (O) _C cyclically. Let M be the circle tangent to (O) _A, (O) _B, (O) _C that encompasses them; call M the . Let M' be the circle tangent to (O) _A, (O) _B, (O) _C that is encompassed by each of them; call M' the . Then X_8160 is the center of M, and X_8161 is the center of M'. The contact points of M with (O) _A, (O) _B, (O) _C are the vertices of a triangle perspective to ABC, with perspector X_1343. Likewise, the contact points of M' with (O) _A, (O) _B, (O) _C are the vertices of a triangle perspective to ABC, with perspector X_1342. (Based on notes from Angel Montesdeoca, October 2, 2015)

no: (Contributed by Angel Montesceoca, Ocftober 9, 2015) Let ABC be a triangle and k a real number. Let B_{A} on line AB and C_{A} on line AC be points such that B_{A}C_{A} is parallel to BC at distance \|kr(A)\|, where r(A) is the inradius of triangle :g:`AB_{A}C_{A} << A B_A C_A >>`. Points C_{B}, A_{B}, A_{C}, B_{C} are defined cyclically. The six points B_{A}, C_{A}, C_{B}, A_{B}, A_{C}, B_{C} lie on a conic, with barycentric equation
bc - \(a^{2}\) : ba - bc : ca - cb ab - ac : ac - \(b^{2}\) : cb - ca ac - ab : bc - ba : ba - \(c^{2}\)
